strategies.overview: Drakloak is NFE's premier Ghost-type and an elite choice for speed control. Boasting the highest unboosted Speed in the metagame alongside a variety of utility options, Drakloak is an excellent phazer capable of disrupting attackers and walls alike with Dragon Tail, Night Shade, and status while also doubling as a spinblocker. Additionally, Drakloak is a great wallbreaker, leveraging its high-powered coverage and Speed to disrupt foes expecting utility sets, like Gabite and Naclstack. However, its frailty and typing make it very vulnerable to Knock Off, making matchups like Monferno and Thwackey difficult. Night Shade sets are walled by Normal-types like Dunsparce and Girafarig, while Choice Specs sets can suffer from being too weak even against foes like Tinkatuff and utility Dunsparce.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Status-spreader sets running Thunder Wave or Will-O-Wisp alongside Hex capitalize on Drakloak's support capabilities. Drakloak can run a dual screens set alongside Light Clay, capitalizing on its deep utility movepool with options like U-turn, Thunder Wave, and Curse, though Morgrem tends to be the superior dual screens setter, the archetype is uncommon, and Drakloak prefers running offensive or more standard utility sets. Hydro Pump can be used on the Choice Specs set to surprise Piloswine and Naclstack while maintaining good coverage against Fire-types, though it loses out on either Fire Blast's wider overall coverage or U-turn's pivoting. For Utility Drakloak sets, Rocky Helmet is an item option that punishes Quaxwell's Triple Axel and U-turn from Pokemon like Fletchinder and Raboot, and Clear Body can be used to ignore Sticky Web and to block Parting Shot from Morgrem.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Drakloak heavily struggles against Fairy-types like Tinkatuff and Clefairy with both sets, with only Fire Blast being threatening against physically bulky Tinkatuff variants. Clefairy particularly does well, recovering any damage with ease and disrupting Drakloak with its own utility moves. However, the RestTalk set can outlast the Fairy-types, though it doesn't enjoy losing Eviolite to Knock Off and being locked into unfavorable moves with Encore.

Normal-types: Dunsparce is one of the most consistent answers to Drakloak, being immune to Night Shade and forcing it to use Draco Meteor or Dragon Tail phazing to threaten notable damage. Dunsparce can recover the damage away with Slack Off and use Drakloak as setup fodder. Girafarig is similarly effective against Night Shade sets but struggles a lot more against Choice Specs sets.

Piloswine: Piloswine can tank any hit from Drakloak with ease and revenge kill it; Ice Shard against Choice Specs sets requires minimal chip damage for it to KO.

Dark-types: While relatively uncommon, Dark-types like Alolan Grimer, Vullaby, and Pawniard perform excellently against Drakloak, resisting at least one of its STAB moves and threatening it back with their own. Alolan Grimer and Vullaby can stomach even Choice Specs-boosted attacks and fire back with Knock Off, while Pawniard resists Drakloak's STAB moves and can KO it first with Sucker Punch.

Naclstack: While similarly uncommon, Naclstack is immune to status conditions and can whittle Drakloak down with Salt Cure, only fearing the rare Hydro Pump.

Faster Pokemon and Priority Moves: While Drakloak is the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, it struggles to deal with Choice Scarf users like Frogadier and Girafarig that can outspeed it with a boost. Sucker Punch users like Raboot and Pignite remain similarly dangerous in spite of their lower Speed tiers, alongside Piloswine's Ice Shard.

movesets.name: Utility Pivot
movesets.description:
Drakloak is the fastest Pokemon in the tier and helps revenge kill offensive threats such as Frogadier and Girafarig while blocking Quaxwell from removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Draco Meteor is Drakloak's strongest move for immediate power, while Hex does consistent damage after status has been spread on the opposing team. Thunder Wave allows Drakloak to spread paralysis to its common checks such as Tinkatuff and Dunsparce, potentially creating some key opportunities in long games. Will-O-Wisp helps deal with Piloswine and Krokorok, which cannot be paralyzed, as well as other physical attackers like Thwackey, providing a more consistent effect with burn compared to paralysis. Drakloak also serves as a fantastic offensive pivot with U-turn, as it comes in on defensive Pokemon such as Dusclops, Koffing, and Quaxwell and pivots on its common answers to bring in wallbreakers such as Pignite and Thwackey. Eviolite is an option to give Drakloak more bulk; however, it dislikes hazards being up, especially Toxic Spikes, which hinder it permanently. In addition to Eviolite, Drakloak can use Cursed Body, but Infiltrator is usually the preferred option, giving Drakloak a good matchup against dual screens hyper offense teams and letting it hit Pokemon behind Substitute such as Servine and Girafarig.

Drakloak perfectly fits in teams that lack speed control, especially if paired with wallbreakers like Pignite, Fraxure, and Piloswine, which make great partners, as they appreciate its ability to pivot on defensive Pokemon to give them opportunities to wallbreak while threatening Drakloak's common answers such as Scraggy and Hisuian Sliggoo. Pokemon that use pivoting moves such as Raboot, Monferno, and Thwackey also make great teammates for Drakloak, helping to keep momentum and applying offensive pressure with ease. Stealth Rock users such as Tinkatuff, Piloswine, and Krokorok and Spikes users like Quilladin and Glimmet appreciate Drakloak's ability to block Quaxwell from spinning and keep entry hazards on the field, allowing them to make consistent progress. Drakloak is weak to Piloswine, so Pokemon that consistently check Piloswine are much appreciated, such as Quaxwell, Seadra, and Dunsparce. Knock Off absorbers such as Koffing and Tinkatuff cover Drakloak's weakness to Knock Off. Drakloak appreciates Pokemon that are able to break special walls like Pignite, Krokorok, and Piloswine.

movesets.name: RestTalk
movesets.description:
The combination of Night Shade and Dragon Tail alongside Drakloak's high Speed and valued typing makes it a premier phazer. RestTalk gives it longevity, making it a good status absorber for burns, paralysis, and poison from status users like Koffing and Hattrem, all while allowing Drakloak to continue phazing, spinblocking, and chipping foes. 216 Speed EVs enable Drakloak to outspeed non-Choice Scarf Frogadier and make it the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, while the 40 EVs in Defense enable it to always survive Knock Off from Life Orb Thwackey and Icicle Crash from non-Choice Band Piloswine. While Drakloak's abilities are all useful, Clear Body stands out by not having Drakloak's Speed be lowered by Sticky Web, as well as stopping Memento from lead Glimmet sets.

Drakloak tends to fit on many balanced and bulky teams, being integral to stopping Rapid Spin attempts from Quaxwell. Entry hazard setters like Piloswine, Frogadier, and Quilladin all pair well with it, forming a hazard-stacking core while providing utility in their own right. Fairy-types like Tinkatuff and Clefairy can be tricky to deal with, able to lock Drakloak into unfavorable moves with Encore and chip away at it with their utility moves. Checks to them like Gabite and Ivysaur can significantly threaten them back while taking paralysis relatively well. Normal-types like Dunsparce and Girafarig are immune to Night Shade and can threaten super effective coverage or powerful Psychic-type STAB moves; Steel-types like the aforementioned Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo are excellent answers to them. While Drakloak has a good defensive profile, its frailty makes it unreliable at answering certain Pokemon like Monferno and Thwackey; Koffing makes for an excellent Knock Off absorber while completing hazard cores with Toxic Spikes and potentially stealing other Eviolites with Thief. Wallbreakers and revenge killers like Fraxure and Raboot can take advantage of Drakloak's spinblocking capabilities to more easily break down defensive titans like Quaxwell and Koffing from the accumulated residual damage. Given Drakloak's vulnerability to Piloswine, checks to it like Quaxwell and Dunsparce are also appreciated; Quaxwell can pivot and remove hazards with Rapid Spin.

movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Choice Specs Drakloak is an effective wallbreaker and, with a Timid nature, speed control option, using its powerful STAB moves in conjunction with great coverage options to break through even the sturdiest of checks. Hydro Pump can be used to break past Fire- and Ground-types like Pignite and Piloswine, while Surf can be used as a less powerful but more reliable option. Thunderbolt is an effective coverage option that can zap Water-types like Quaxwell and Wartortle efficiently. Alternatively, if teams have status-spreading support from teammates like Glare Servine, Toxic Spikes Koffing, Glare or Body Slam Dunsparce, Drakloak can opt to use Hex, which is more powerful than Shadow Ball against foes with status. Infiltrator can prevent Substitute users like Wartortle and offensive Gabite from being safe against Drakloak, allowing it to function more effectively as a revenge killer. A Modest nature can help Drakloak break more efficiently at the cost of being slower than Frogadier and Raboot; it does secure a 2HKO on Quaxwell with Draco Meteor after taking entry hazard chip damage, which can be valuable on sets without Thunderbolt.

Choice Specs Drakloak functions best on balance and bulky offense teams that have Knock Off and entry hazard support, using its powerful STAB attacks to clean late-game once its checks like Dunsparce and Tinkatuff are worn down. Clefairy and especially Tinkatuff are excellent teammates for Drakloak, providing Knock Off and Stealth Rock support to go along with their immunity to Dragon-type attacks from opposing Drakloak and other threats like Choice Scarf Gabite and Frogadier. Monferno similarly provides Knock Off and Stealth Rock support while being able to threaten Tinkatuff. Quaxwell can provide hazard removal, check Piloswine, and give Drakloak safe entry points with its Flip Turn. Piloswine is a great teammate because it provides Stealth Rock support, while Drakloak can spinblock and check Quaxwell for Piloswine in return. Drakloak has to be wary of Dunsparce and Piloswine, as both can tank its attacks and use the opportunity to dish out high damage in return. Wartortle is another problem for Drakloak, as it can use the Special Attack drop from Draco Meteor as an opportunity to set up with Shell Smash. Teammates that can help with these threats include Dunsparce, which can help sponge attacks from Piloswine, and Thwackey, which can provide safe entry points with U-turn and has the powerful Grassy Glide to take down Piloswine and Wartortle if they take some chip damage first. Pignite is a great teammate, as it can use its STAB attacks to help break through bulky Normal- and Steel-types, such as Dunsparce and Tinkatuff, while providing Knock Off support. Raboot can also help in these endeavors; it lacks Knock Off but can still use U-turn to give Drakloak entry points against Pokemon like Quaxwell. Koffing can help check Clefairy while boosting the damage of Hex by spreading Toxic Spikes, and other status spreaders like Glare Servine and Thunder Wave can Tinkatuff also provide this support.
